what: Badger Meter makes water meters and the software and communication networks that let utilities read them remotely. It also sells water quality sensors and flow measurement products for industry.
customers: Water utilities across North America that replace mechanical meters with smart meters, and industrial customers.
money: Smart water meters, cellular radios and the BEACON software platform.
Flow and quality measurement for industry.
moat: Its cellular-based reading system avoids the need for utilities to build their own networks, and its software creates recurring revenue and switching costs.
risks: Over the last twelve months revenue and profit dipped from 2025 levels, which may mean replacement demand is cooling.
Utilities buy in large projects, which makes quarters lumpy.
At 34–38 times earnings, the valuation assumes steady growth.
Tariffs on components can pressure margins.
opportunities: Revenue grew every year from $505M in 2021 to $917M in 2025, and net income more than doubled.
No debt and steady free cash flow.
Many US utilities still have old mechanical meters to replace.
Software and data services add recurring revenue.
watch: Order trends from utilities and gross margin.
view: Badger Meter has been one of the best industrial compounders of the decade: revenue nearly doubled and profit more than doubled from 2021 to 2025, with no debt and rising margins, as utilities replaced mechanical meters with smart ones.

The latest twelve months show the first dip, with revenue and profit below 2025. That may be lumpiness in utility orders or the start of a slower phase as the replacement cycle matures. At 34–38 times earnings, the market still prices it as a steady grower.
This turns on whether the dip is temporary. I think the long-term opportunity remains large, but at this valuation I would wait for evidence that growth has resumed.
bull: Meter replacement continues for years and software revenue lifts margins further.
bear: The replacement cycle slows and the premium multiple contracts.
